newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Association of Southeast Asian Nations has decided to postpone indefinitely Cambodia's membership but will still admit Burma and Laos as full members at its annual meeting in Kuala Lumpur later this month. Hun Sen yesterday declared himself Cambodia's "captain", but ASEAN made it clear that it still recognises ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh as a co-premier in Cambodia and will treat him as equal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- The proposal by charter drafters to liberalise the TV and radio industry is expected to be shot down today. The draft vetting panel has agreed to allow the military to retain their frequencies for security purposes. The vetting panel has agreed during an informal meeting to add a clause to Article 39 which will allow the military to retain its radio and TV bands. (THE NATION)

- Hopewell (Thailand) Co has made a U-turn announcement by promising again that part of its elevated mass transit system can begin services before the 13th Asian Games in Bangkok in December next year. The company earlier reported that the system would not be operational before the start of the Games. (BANGKOK POST)

- The state-run Property Loan Management Organisation (PLMO) will include property loans collateralised by land banks under its fold. The decision follows the approval in principle by its board of directors because such loans have been estimated to be around 50 billion baht. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Only one or two of the 16 suspended finance companies are likely to meet today's deadline to submit a business revival plan to the Bank of Thailand. The others are unlikely to submit plans to the central bank as their major shareholders have refused to discount the finance firms' assets to reflect the real net worth of the companies. (BANGKOK POST)
